This page maps the full arc of the DP Music course. Use it to orient yourself at the start of a new term or to explain the course structure to a parent, administrator, or new student.

---

## How the Course Is Structured

DP Music runs over two years and requires you to work simultaneously across four IB components (five if you are HL). The two years have different centres of gravity:

- **Year 1** is organized around *thematic units*. Each unit introduces a musical tradition, asks you to analyze it carefully, perform within it, and respond to it creatively. The units are designed to give you a wide range of musical encounters that you will draw on when you build your IB portfolios.
- **Year 2** shifts toward *portfolio development and refinement*. The themes from Year 1 become the source material you investigate, experiment with, and present formally for IB assessment.

The four IB components run throughout both years, but their weight increases significantly in Year 2 as final submissions approach.

## Pre-IB: Foundation Year (G10)

Pre-IB Music establishes the skills and habits that DP builds on. The year is organized around a single anchoring question: *who are you as a musician, and what does music mean to you?*

**About Me** — Students select four songs that represent their musical identity, research them, and present their choices to the class. This playlist becomes source material for the rest of the year.

**Exploring Music** — A focused introduction to musical analysis: elements of music (rhythm, melody, harmony, texture, timbre, structure), and how to listen and write analytically. Remix listening develops the ability to hear convention and variation across styles.

**Creating and Experimenting** — Students compose in a DAW, then perform a genre experiment — taking a song from their About Me playlist and transforming it into a different style. This is the closest Pre-IB equivalent to the DP Experimenting component.

**Performing and Presenting** — Students select, rehearse, and perform a solo piece, writing program notes explaining their interpretive choices. This is the closest Pre-IB equivalent to the DP Presenting component.

---

## DP Year 1: Thematic Exploration

Year 1 is built around four thematic units, each centered on a musical tradition from a specific cultural and historical context. The units progress through four of the IB's Areas of Inquiry (AOIs):

::: {.callout-note}
## Areas of Inquiry (AOIs)
The IB identifies four AOIs that organize how music functions in the world:

- **AOI 1** — Music for sociocultural and political expression
- **AOI 2** — Music for listening and performance
- **AOI 3** — Music for dramatic impact, movement, and screen
- **AOI 4** — Music technology in the modern world
:::

### Sem 1 — AOI 1 Focus

**Unit 1: Music for Social Change** — How has music been used to express political and social dissent? Students analyze protest music traditions, compose in the style, and perform representative works. Core skills: AOI identification and justification, compositional voice, performing practice analysis.

**Unit 2: Music for Ritual** — How does music function in ceremony, liturgy, and collective observance? Students examine traditions ranging from sacred vocal polyphony to ritual drumming. Core skills: contextual analysis, timbral awareness, comparative listening.

### Sem 2 — AOI 3 / AOI 4 Focus

**Unit 3: Music in Theater** — How does music serve drama? Students analyze opera, musical theater, and folk-theatrical traditions. Core skills: text-music relationships, ornamentation, performance interpretation.

**Unit 4: Music in Multimedia** — How does music shape image and interaction? Students study film scoring, advertising, and games. Core skills: compositional technique for media, structural analysis, producing.

### IB Component Work in Year 1

While thematic units are running, IB component work begins:

- **Exploring**: AOI identification, elements analysis, annotated bibliography, harmonic analysis exercises
- **Experimenting**: First creating experiments; performance planning documents; performer experiments begin
- **Presenting**: Program notes; minor compositions; first full drafts by end of year
- **CMM** *(HL)*: Collaborator identification, conceptual planning, music outline, draft composition
- **Performing**: Repertoire selected and locked; regular practice logs; SMART goals; IB Concert (Nov/Dec)

---

## DP Year 2: Component Synthesis

Year 2 is structured around completing and refining each IB component. Thematic exploration continues, but the emphasis shifts to building coherent portfolios from the material gathered in Year 1.

### Sem 1 — Deepening and Drafting

Each component moves from exploratory work to a full draft:

- **Performing** — IB Concert performance; recital repertoire challenges; SMART goal cycle with recording evidence
- **Exploring** — Formal analysis; deeper contextual writing; draft exploration submitted for feedback
- **Experimenting** — Performer experiments completed; creating and experimenting drafts submitted
- **Presenting** — Performance Level Recording; full draft with all sections complete
- **CMM** *(HL)* — Collaborator update; collaboration video; progress documentation

### Sem 2 — Final Submissions and IB Recital

All components reach their final form and are submitted to the IB. The IB Recital takes place in March.

---

## IB Assessment Summary

::: {.callout-important}
## What Gets Submitted to the IB

| Component | What's Submitted | SL/HL |
|---|---|---|
| **Exploring Music in Context** | Written portfolio (2,000 words) + creating exercise (32 bars / 1 min) + performed adaptation | Both |
| **Experimenting with Music** | Written portfolio (1,500 words) + experiments (creating and/or performing) | Both |
| **Presenting Music** | Performance recordings + score/production documentation | Both |
| **Contemporary Music Maker** | Commissioned/created music + written support material | HL only |
| **Performing** | IB Recital (recorded in school) | Both |

All components are externally assessed by IB examiners. Performing is assessed by a visiting examiner.
:::

::: {.callout-tip}

## SL vs HL

The course is available at Standard Level (SL) and Higher Level (HL). The components are identical; HL adds the **Contemporary Music Maker** component, which requires you to create a substantial original work in collaboration with at least one other musician, and to document the collaboration process.

HL students should expect the CMM to run in parallel with all four shared components throughout both years. It is not an add-on to complete at the end — it requires sustained engagement from the beginning of Year 1.
